reproduction_target: Comparative/population genomics of 61 Diutina catenulata strains: Illumina read QC, bwa-mem2 mapping to the CBS 565T reference, GATK/vcftools SNP calling and filtering, IQ-TREE phylogeny, fastStructure/CLUMPP/poppr/ade4/PopGenome population structure and diversity statistics, transposon content quantification (bwa-mem2 + featureCounts + samtools), synteny and rearrangement analysis (SynChro, MUMmer4, circlize), and characterization/mining/phylogeny of the novel Dici DNA transposon family (InterPro, InterProScan, PSIPRED, PSORT II, TBLASTN/BLASTN, MAFFT, ClipKIT, IQ-TREE, seqinr). Strain isolation/identification, flow cytometry, PFGE karyotyping, DNA extraction and Illumina library prep + sequencing are wet-lab (W, out of scope for computational reproduction).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, built from the bioRxiv v1 JATS XML Methods section (retrieved by curl; WebFetch of the .source.xml returned HTTP 403). Section 4 (Methods) covers 4.1-4.14. Genome assembly and annotation of the five long-read-assembled genomes are NOT described anywhere in the main Methods text (assembly/annotation statistics are deferred to Supplementary Table 3, and the supplementary PDF 'Supplementary results, materials, procedures and figures' was not part of the retrieved full text); this is recorded as one blocked step (C1). There is no Data availability or Code availability statement in the main text; sequencing and assembly accession numbers are stated only to be inside Supplementary Table 1, and no accession is enumerated in the retrievable prose. No author analysis-code repository is cited anywhere in the paper; the only repository URL in the text is the Genoscope tool dependency github.com/institut-de-genomique/fastxtend. Wet-lab steps counted in W, not verdicted.

steps.label: Genome assembly and annotation of the five D. catenulata genomes — no assembler, annotator, sequencing technology, version or parameter is described in the main Methods; only assembly/annotation statistics are referenced (Supplementary Table 3)

Illumina read trimming / quality filtering with in-house Genoscope software based on the FastX package (github.com/institut-de-genomique/fastxtend) — Q<20 end trimming, adapter/primer removal, reads <30 nt discarded; no version, no release tag
phiX read-pair removal with the SOAP aligner against phiX174 (GenBank NC_001422.1) — no SOAP version, no alignment parameters
Short-read mapping of 61 strains with bwa-mem2 version 2.0pre1 to the CBS 565T genome, with the 388 kb chromosome F segmental duplication (DICA0_F:3198109-3586457) masked
Variant calling with GATK v4.5.0.0 HaplotypeCaller (--sample-ploidy 2, --emit-ref-confidence GVCF) plus hard filtering 'according to GATK best practice' (thresholds not enumerated in prose)
SNP filtering with vcftools version v0.1.16 (--minGQ 30 --minDP 30 --maf 0.03 --max-missing 0.9)
Custom removal of clustered heterozygous SNPs (>7 heterozygous SNPs within a 1,000 bp window) — no tool or script named
Conversion of the 351,942-SNP VCF to FASTA with IUPAC ambiguity codes for heterozygous positions — no tool or script named
Maximum-likelihood SNP phylogeny with IQ-TREE v2.3.1 (-T AUTO -m MFP, ModelFinder model selection, -B 1000 ultrafast bootstrap)
VCF-to-PED conversion and LD pruning with PLINK v1.90b7.2 (--indep-pairwise 50 5 0.5), yielding 34,101 SNPs
Population structure inference with fastStructure — 20 runs, prior set to 'simple'; no version pinned, K range not stated
Summarization of the 20 fastStructure runs with CLUMPP v1.1.2 (algorithm/parameters not stated)
Plotting of structure results in R v4.5.0 — plotting script not provided
AMOVA for population differentiation with the R package poppr v2.9.7
Permutation tests via the randtest function of the R package ade4 v1.7-23 (number of permutations and RNG seed not stated)
Population genetics statistics (pi, dXY, FST, Tajima's D) with the R package PopGenome v2.7.7 in 10,000 bp windows, averaged genome-wide

Re-mapping of the 61 short-read sets with bwa-mem2 against a FASTA containing one copy per transposon family (consensus FASTA itself not deposited as a named file; element coordinates in Supplementary Table 6)
Per-element read counting with featureCounts v2.0.6 (Subread package) — counting options not stated
Total mapped-read counts with samtools v.1.15.1 (samtools view -c -G 13 -F 256) on the bwa-mem2 BAM files
Synteny block reconstruction from pairwise comparisons of the five annotated genomes with SynChro — no version, no parameters (e.g. delta value) stated
Global genome alignments with the MUMmer4 package, filtered with delta-filter (-l 5000 -m) and coordinates extracted with show-coords — no MUMmer4 version pinned
Circular representation of chromosomal rearrangements in R with the package circlize v0.4.16 — plotting script not provided
Functional analysis of the three Dici protein sequences with the InterPro web service (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/interpro) — no release version, no access date
Protein secondary structure prediction with PSIPRED version 4 (web service, default parameters implied)
Nuclear localization signal prediction with PSORT II (http://psort.hgc.jp) — no version, no parameters

Taxonomic mining of Dici transposases with TBLASTN (version 2.15.0) against NCBI nt and Eukaryote RefSeq Genomes nucleotide databases (downloaded 23/05/2025), E-value cutoff 1e-10; queries Dici1 (DICA0_E02476) and Dici2 (DICA4_A06172)
DDE catalytic domain confirmation with InterProScan version 5.71-102.0 (--applications PFAM, domain PF13358)
Alignment of best-hit sequences with 2-kb flanking regions using MAFTT [sic] v7.453 (--maxiterate 1000 --genafpair)
Manual checking of transposon boundaries for terminal inverted repeats (TIR) and target site duplications (TSD) — human curation step, no script, no decision criteria recorded

Copy-number estimation by searching each transposon sequence against its host genome with BLASTN (E-value cutoff 1e-40; hits kept if >40% in size and >80% identity) — no BLASTN version stated at this step (2.15.0 is stated only for TBLASTN)
Multiple sequence alignment of transposase sequences (full-length or catalytic domain) with MAFFT (--maxiterate 1000 --globalpair); version stated as v7.453 earlier in Methods
Alignment trimming with ClipKIT version 1.3.0 (-m kpi-smart-gap)
Transposase maximum-likelihood phylogeny with IQ-TREE version 2.3.1 (-T 10 -mset LG,JTT,WAG,Dayhoff,NQ.yeast,Q.yeast; ModelFinder; -B 1000 ultrafast bootstrap)
Family-wise pairwise identity matrices from the MAFFT alignments with the R package seqinr (v4.2-36), averaged per transposon family pair

headline.static_readiness: 0/34 (0%) — stage1 ceiling only, no R★ (R★ needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 22/34 computational steps — these carry exact prose version pins (bwa-mem2 2.0pre1, GATK 4.5.0.0, vcftools 0.1.16, IQ-TREE 2.3.1, PLINK 1.90b7.2, CLUMPP 1.1.2, R 4.5.0, poppr 2.9.7, ade4 1.7-23, PopGenome 2.7.7, featureCounts 2.0.6, samtools 1.15.1, circlize 0.4.16, PSIPRED 4, TBLASTN 2.15.0, InterProScan 5.71-102.0, MAFFT 7.453, ClipKIT 1.3.0, seqinr 4.2-36) but no environment closure of any kind. 9/34 steps cap at NI because no version is pinned (in-house fastxtend-based trimming, SOAP, custom het-SNP filter, VCF-to-FASTA conversion, fastStructure, MUMmer4, InterPro web, PSORT II, BLASTN copy-number). 3/34 are blocked (X): genome assembly/annotation is described nowhere in the main Methods, SynChro is named with neither version nor parameters (params axis 0), and the transposon boundary determination is explicit manual curation. No lockfile, container, or conda spec is claimed; no author analysis-code repository exists, so even at Stage 2 no step can exceed RI.
headline.coverage: 34 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 JATS Methods (sections 4.6-4.14) plus one blocked step for the undocumented assembly/annotation. 6 wet-lab steps (strain isolation and culture, D1/D2 + ITS sequencing identification, flow cytometry ploidy, PFGE/CHEF karyotyping, genomic DNA extraction, Illumina library prep and NovaSeq 6000 sequencing) counted in W and out of computational-reproduction scope.

gaps.where: Whole paper — no Code availability statement
gaps.missing: The paper cites no author analysis-code repository (no GitHub/GitLab/Zenodo/Software Heritage). The only repository URL in the text is a Genoscope tool dependency (https://github.com/institut-de-genomique/fastxtend). No pipeline driver, no filtering scripts (het-SNP clustering, VCF-to-FASTA conversion), and no plotting scripts (R structure plots, circlize) are provided.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the analysis scripts and pipeline driver in a public repository with a tagged release archived to Zenodo, and cite the DOI in a Code availability statement.

gaps.missing: No environment lockfile, container image/digest, or conda/env specification is claimed anywhere. Exact versions are given per tool, but there is no dependency closure (BLAST+/Subread/HTSlib/R library stack, Python for fastStructure, etc.), so capture_claim is exact_pins_partial at best.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock/pixi lockfile or a container digest pinning the full toolchain (bwa-mem2, GATK, vcftools, IQ-TREE, PLINK, CLUMPP, fastStructure, MUMmer4, SynChro, Subread, samtools, BLAST+, InterProScan, MAFFT, ClipKIT, R + poppr/ade4/PopGenome/circlize/seqinr).

gaps.missing: No version pins for the in-house FastX-based trimming software, SOAP aligner, fastStructure, SynChro, MUMmer4, the InterPro web service, PSORT II, and the BLASTN run used for copy-number estimation. The NCBI nt / RefSeq download date (23/05/2025) is given, which is good practice, but the databases themselves are not archived.
gaps.how_to_close: Pin a version (or commit/release tag) for every tool and web service, and archive or version-stamp the NCBI database snapshots used.

gaps.where: Data availability / sequencing and assembly accessions
gaps.missing: There is no Data availability statement in the main text. Accession numbers for the raw sequencing reads and the assembled genomes are stated only to be contained in Supplementary Table 1 (and Supplementary Table 9 for sequencing statistics); no accession, BioProject, or repository is enumerated in the retrievable prose, so the entry point for every computational step is unverifiable at Stage 1. Additionally, the transposon consensus FASTA used in the copy-number/content quantification (C17) is not deposited as a named file.
gaps.how_to_close: Add an explicit Data availability statement in the main text with the BioProject/ENA/GenBank accessions, and deposit the transposon consensus sequences and the filtered VCF (351,942 SNPs) as citable supplementary data.

gaps.where: Steps C1, C5, C11, C12, C15, C18, C20
gaps.missing: Parameter under-specification: GATK 'hard filtering according to GATK best practice' does not enumerate thresholds; fastStructure K range is not given; CLUMPP algorithm/parameters are not given; ade4 randtest permutation count and RNG seed are not given; featureCounts counting options are not given; SynChro delta/parameters are not given; assembly and annotation have no parameters at all.
gaps.how_to_close: State every non-default parameter, RNG seed, and threshold in Methods or, preferably, in the published scripts.

gaps.where: Step C1 — genome assembly and annotation
gaps.missing: The five assembled and annotated genomes underpin the synteny, rearrangement, and transposon-characterization analyses, but the main Methods never describe how they were assembled or annotated (no sequencing technology, assembler, polisher, or annotation pipeline named). Only summary statistics are referenced (Supplementary Table 3).
gaps.how_to_close: Add an assembly and annotation Methods subsection naming and versioning every tool and parameter, or point explicitly to the supplementary procedures section where it lives.

gaps.missing: Transposon boundaries (TIR/TSD) were 'checked manually', with no recorded decision criteria and no curated output file, so this step is not machine-reproducible and the downstream copy-number and phylogeny inputs depend on it.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the curated boundary coordinates and the criteria applied, or replace the manual step with a scripted TIR/TSD detection with stated thresholds.

gaps.missing: Strain isolation and culture, D1/D2 + ITS taxonomic identification by Sanger sequencing, flow cytometry ploidy estimation (C6 Accuri), PFGE/CHEF karyotyping, genomic DNA extraction, and Illumina library preparation + NovaSeq 6000 sequencing are physical steps, out of scope for computational reproduction; counted in W and not verdicted.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness; the reproducible entry point would be the deposited raw reads and assemblies once their accessions are published.
